zac_language.numbers_framing: Leads with the net payout figure first (~£2,411/month average), then unbundles it into the three deduction categories (platform fees, 15% management, ~18% cleaning/laundry), states a worst-to-best monthly range (£1,900-£3,600) rather than a single number, and backs the conservative framing with a real case study (a Manchester 3-bed) where actual year-one results landed almost exactly on the worst-case projection given at the time — building credibility through demonstrated conservatism rather than optimistic promises.
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Doesn't dismiss the competing advisor's contrasting approach — validates it first ('I would guarantee you he's going to list on an online platform as well'), then reframes the disagreement as risk diversification rather than a right-vs-wrong choice (platform as stable base, direct bookings as the icing on top), and closes the loop by tying it back to the lead's own stated long-term investment horizon.

profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For analytical-evaluator PURCH leads who are actively cross-shopping advice from other operators or advisors, proactively surface the platform-vs-direct-booking philosophical difference early and frame it as risk diversification (not an inferior alternative) before the lead has to raise it as a direct comparison; lean on hard, verifiable case-study proof points early, since this archetype anchors trust in checkable data over persuasive framing.
